newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-DISAPPOINTED PEDROSO FALLS SHORT OF PERSONAL GOAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DISAPPOINTED PEDROSO FALLS SHORT OF PERSONAL GOAL.

text.p: Ivan Pedroso proclaimed himself disappointed with his performance on Tuesday despite retaining his world long jump title.

"I wanted to put a big mark out in the first round and then go all out to be the first man to jump beyond nine metres," Pedroso said. "I managed to do well with my first effort but after that my technique let me down.
"I was always trying for a new world record."
The current world best of 8.95 metres was set by American Mike Powell at the 1991 Tokyo world championships.
Pedroso, 25, had to settle for victory with his first effort of 8.42 metres.
He followed up that mark with four no-jumps and a modest leap in the final round with the gold medal already won.
"It will take some special conditions for me to go beyond nine metres. I can do it but it was not going to be today," he said.

Pedroso identified the lack of a helpful following breeze as the main reason why he won with the poorest winning performance since the championships started in 1983. Another factor was the lack of pressure from his rivals.
The Cuban did get near the nine metre mark on one occasion.
A huge effort in the fourth round saw him cut the sand around that point but half his foot was over the take-off board and the jump was ruled a foul.
Pedroso led throughout all six rounds but behind him an enthralling competition developed for the minor medals.
American Erick Walder jumped 8.29 in the first round and improved to 8.36 in the fourth before finishing with 8.38 with his final jump to secure the silver.
Russia's Kiril Sosunov and Jamaica's James Beckford swapped third place on four occasions before the Russian took the bronze medal with his final round 8.18.
Pedroso was unconcerned that anyone was capable of jumping further than him and barely gave Walder's last round jump a second glance.
"If anyone had overtaken me, I would have controlled my running and got the gold medal back," he said.
